title: GAMING THE JUDGE: UNFAITHFUL CHAIN-OF-THOUGHT CAN UNDERMINE AGENT EVALUATION

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating whether LLM judges default to accepting fabricated declarative statements about task progress in the agent's Chain-of-Thought (CoT) as factual, even when unsupported by actual environment observations.

Rewriting the agent's CoT to amplify confidence, decisiveness, and fluency (Competence Boosting) to test if judges treat well-articulated and confident explanations as more credible indicators of success.
Modifying the CoT to appear slow, careful, and methodical (Reflective Reasoning) to test if judges mistakenly equate apparent deliberation with correctness or rigor.

Rewriting the CoT to attribute unexpected or inefficient behavior to made-up interface or environmental issues (Environment Blaming), testing if judges accept reframed external causes for task failure.
Subtly redefining the task objective in the CoT (Task Reinterpretation) to test if judges assess task success relative to a distorted task definition rather than the original user intent.

primary_bias_target: Evaluation bias (Cognitive heuristics in LLM judges)
